messages:
incident-bot: [PAGER] cb-serving-prod: sudden 95p token latency spike and KV eviction rate increase in region us-west-2. Impacting multiple routes. Dash: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/cb/latency?orgId=1

Alice Chen: acked, oncall. seeing 95p up ~2.3x and 99p up ~4x for last 12m. KV cache evictions jumped from ~200/s -> 4k/s.

Ben Ortiz: any recent config rollouts?

Carla Mendez: Rolling config: continuous_batch.target_microbatch=64 -> 128 rolled 3h ago to improve throughput for big requests. Also pushed prefetch heuristics tweak.

Dave Kwon: hypothesis: larger microbatch target + high concurrency => longer queueing -> KV cache churn (hot key sets changed) -> eviction cascade -> downstream request slowdown. Typical.

Alice Chen: can we toggle back the target to 64 for affected pools? Which pool IDs are hitting it?

Ben Ortiz: impacted pools: pool-cb-usw2-3, pool-cb-usw2-7. I'm running `rbacctl get pool pool-cb-usw2-3 --json` now.

Ben Ortiz: result: avg_concurrency=220, inflight_q_len=180, microbatch_target=128.

Carla Mendez: quick mitigation: lower microbatch_target to 48 and enable cb_prefetch_disable=true for these pools. Rolling a hotfix now.

Elise Patel: (+1) do a canary on pool-cb-usw2-7 first (lowest traffic). If stable, roll faster.

Dave Kwon: command I ran to patch pool (shared):
```
PATCH /api/v1/pools/pool-cb-usw2-7
{ "microbatch_target": 48, "cb_prefetch_disable": true }
```
Applied at 1767771900.

Alice Chen: metrics post-patch (5m after): 95p latency down 28%, KV evictions down to ~600/s. For the canary, ok to roll to pool-cb-usw2-3.

Ben Ortiz: rolling to pool-cb-usw2-3 now. patch at 1767772100.

pagerduty-bot: Incident annotated: priority=P2, pager duty alert cleared for oncall after mitigation.

Carla Mendez: monitoring heatmap: tail latency still elevated for some large-seq customers. Likely manual prefetched caches warm up slower after change.

Elise Patel: customer impact note: outage window 1767771234 -> 1767772300. Affected customers: 5 enterprise customers saw >30% increase in p95 token latency, 2 reported degraded UI. No data loss.

Alice Chen: next steps: 1) keep microbatch_target=48 for 2h, 2) run KV cache warmup job for high-q customers, 3) add guardrail to rollout that prevents microbatch_target increases when avg_concurrency>150.

Dave Kwon: created quick PR: `cb/guardrails-prevent-large-microbatch-on-hot-pools` (link: https://git.redwood.ai/cb/+/2345) — aims to block config rollouts that set target_microbatch>80 when pool concurrency>150.

Ben Ortiz: rolling observation window: will check 1h and 3h graphs, will update.

Alice Chen: passing to next oncall (overnight). Summary for handoff:
- Root cause: config rollout increased microbatch_target + prefetch tweak -> under high concurrency caused queueing, KV cache churn and eviction cascade -> latency cliff.
- Mitigation applied: reduced microbatch_target to 48, disabled prefetch for affected pools, warmed KV caches.
- Customer impact: elevated p95/p99 for ~86 minutes, 5 customers impacted, 2 reported visible degradation.
- Followups: PR for rollout guardrails, runback test for prefetch heuristics, postmortem doc and RCA.

Carla Mendez: tagging SRE and Release for postmortem. I've opened incident ticket INC-2026-0423 and assigned to SRE.

Elise Patel: handoff ack. I'll monitor overnight and escalate if anything reappears.

Alice Chen: thanks team :thumbsup: — closing the active pager. I'll draft the customer-facing blurb and sync with support.

Ben Ortiz: quick note for postmortem: capture full KV eviction traces and per-pool microbatch distribution. Also add synthetic load test to replicate high-concurrency large-seq scenario.

Alice Chen: last check at 1767774600 shows stability. handing off now. 

Elise Patel: ack, thanks.
